_meta.description: Step-by-step guided complaint checklists per situation category. Every step is labeled as general information. Edit this file to update guidance without touching code.
_meta.reviewedBy: Initial setup — requires legal review before launch
_meta.disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice. Verify all information with qualified legal counsel.

cyber_harassment.title: Cyber Harassment — What To Do
cyber_harassment.urgentNote: If you are in immediate danger, call 112 (Police) or 1930 (Cyber Crime Helpline) right now.

steps.title: Document Everything Immediately
steps.description: Take screenshots of all abusive messages, posts, or content before they can be deleted.
details: Screenshot the content showing the sender's username/profile and timestamp
Save the URL/link of the content if it's on a website or social media
If it's a video or audio, screen-record with date and time visible on screen
Save complete chat threads — not just individual messages
Note the platform(s) where the harassment occurred

steps.title: Preserve Digital Evidence
steps.description: Store your evidence securely so it cannot be tampered with or lost.
details: Upload screenshots and recordings to SafeStep's Evidence Vault — each file gets a SHA-256 hash and timestamp
Do NOT edit or crop screenshots — courts need originals
If possible, save the page as a PDF using your browser's Print-to-PDF feature
Keep a written log of dates, times, and what happened
Back up evidence on a device the harasser cannot access

steps.title: Report on the Platform
steps.description: Report the abusive content/account on the platform where it occurred.
details: Use the platform's built-in report function (usually under a three-dot menu or flag icon)
Select the most specific violation category available
Note the report reference number or take a screenshot of the confirmation
Under IT Rules 2021, platforms must acknowledge complaints within 24 hours and resolve within 15 days
For intimate/sexual images, platforms must remove within 24 hours of reporting

steps.title: File a Complaint on Cybercrime Portal
steps.description: India's National Cybercrime Reporting Portal allows online complaint filing.
details: Visit cybercrime.gov.in — the official Government of India portal
Select 'Report Other Cyber Crime' or 'Report Women/Child Related Crime' as appropriate
You'll need: your details, suspect details (if known), incident description, and evidence
After filing, you'll receive an acknowledgment number — save this
You can track complaint status on the same portal using your acknowledgment number

steps.title: File a Police Complaint (FIR/NCR)
steps.description: You have the right to file a First Information Report at any police station.
details: Visit your nearest police station or the Cyber Crime Cell in your city
You have the right to file a Zero FIR at any police station — they cannot refuse
If the police refuse to file an FIR, you can approach the Superintendent of Police or a Magistrate
Request a copy of the FIR — this is your legal right
You can request a female officer to record your statement
If you're uncomfortable going in person, some states allow e-FIR filing
documentsNeeded: Written account of the incident with dates and times
FIR acknowledgment from cybercrime.gov.in (if already filed)

steps.title: Contact Additional Support
steps.description: Reach out to support organizations and helplines for guidance and assistance.
details: Call 1930 — National Cyber Crime Helpline (24/7)
Call 181 — Women's Helpline for women-specific cyber harassment
Contact the National Commission for Women (NCW) — online complaint at ncw.nic.in
Reach out to Cyber Peace Foundation for guidance on cyber safety
Consider consulting a lawyer specializing in cyber law for legal advice

stalking.title: Stalking — What To Do
stalking.urgentNote: If you feel you are in immediate danger from a stalker, call 112 (Police) immediately.

steps.title: Document the Stalking Pattern
steps.description: Keep a detailed log of every stalking incident with dates, times, and locations.
details: Write down every encounter — date, time, location, what happened, any witnesses
Screenshot all unwanted messages, friend requests, and profile views
Save voicemails and record call logs (date, time, duration)
If being followed physically, note times, locations, and the stalker's appearance/vehicle
Document any fake profiles created using your name or photos

steps.title: Secure Your Digital Presence
steps.description: Protect your online accounts and personal information.
details: Change passwords on all social media and email accounts
Enable two-factor authentication everywhere possible
Review and restrict privacy settings on all social platforms
Check for and remove any location-sharing or tracking apps on your phone
Google your own name and phone number to see what's publicly visible
Consider using a VPN for internet browsing

steps.title: File a Police Complaint
steps.description: Stalking is a criminal offence. You have the right to file an FIR.
details: Visit your nearest police station with all documented evidence
You have the right to file a Zero FIR at any police station
Provide the stalking log, screenshots, and any witness information
Request a copy of the FIR immediately
You can request a female officer to record your statement
For cyberstalking, you can also file on cybercrime.gov.in
documentsNeeded: Stalking incident log with dates and details

steps.title: Seek a Protection Order
steps.description: You may be eligible for a protection order to legally prevent the stalker from approaching you.
details: Consult a lawyer about applying for a protection order from a Magistrate
A protection order can prohibit the stalker from contacting or approaching you
Free legal aid is available through District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
Contact your nearest Legal Aid Centre — find it at nalsa.gov.in
Violation of a protection order is a separate criminal offence

steps.title: Contact Support Organizations
steps.description: Get help from organizations that specialize in supporting stalking victims.
details: Call 181 — Women's Helpline (available 24/7)
Call 112 — Emergency services if you feel unsafe
Contact Shakti Shalini helpline for support and guidance
National Commission for Women: file a complaint at ncw.nic.in
Inform trusted friends, family, or colleagues about the situation for safety

online_fraud.title: Online Fraud — What To Do
online_fraud.urgentNote: If money was stolen, call 1930 (Cyber Crime Helpline) immediately — early reporting increases recovery chances.

steps.title: Act Immediately — First 24 Hours Are Critical
steps.description: For financial fraud, speed is essential. Contact your bank and the helpline right away.
details: Call 1930 — National Cyber Crime Helpline — immediately to report financial fraud
Call your bank's fraud helpline and request an immediate block on the compromised account/card
If UPI fraud: open your UPI app → go to transaction history → raise a dispute on the fraudulent transaction
Change passwords for all financial apps and email accounts
Do NOT delete any messages, emails, or transaction notifications — these are evidence

steps.title: Collect and Preserve Evidence
steps.description: Gather all records of the fraudulent transaction and communication.
details: Screenshot all transaction confirmations, SMS alerts, and email notifications
Save any communication with the fraudster (messages, emails, call logs)
Note the fraudster's details: phone number, email, UPI ID, bank account, website URL
Save the link or app listing if it was a fake website or app
Get a bank statement showing the fraudulent transaction
Upload everything to SafeStep's Evidence Vault for timestamped, hashed preservation

steps.title: File on Cybercrime Portal
steps.description: Report the fraud on the official National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
details: Visit cybercrime.gov.in and select 'Report Cyber Crime'
For financial fraud, select 'Online Financial Fraud'
Provide: your bank details (affected account), transaction details, fraudster's information
Upload evidence (screenshots, bank statements)
Save your complaint acknowledgment number for tracking
You can check status anytime on the same portal
documentsNeeded: Fraudster's details (phone, email, UPI ID, etc.)

steps.title: File a Police FIR
steps.description: File a First Information Report at your local police station or Cyber Crime Cell.
details: Visit your nearest police station or Cyber Crime Cell with all evidence
You have the right to file a Zero FIR at any police station
Bring printouts of screenshots, bank statements, and communication records
Mention the cybercrime.gov.in complaint number if you've already filed there
Get a copy of the FIR and note the FIR number

steps.title: Contact Your Bank's Nodal Officer
steps.description: If your bank's initial response is unsatisfactory, escalate to their nodal officer.
details: Every bank has a designated Nodal Officer for fraud complaints — find their details on your bank's website
RBI guidelines state that if fraud is reported within 3 days, the customer's liability is limited
Write a formal complaint email to the nodal officer with all evidence attached
If the bank doesn't resolve within 30 days, escalate to the Banking Ombudsman at rbi.org.in
Keep all correspondence with the bank for your records
steps.authority: Bank Nodal Officer / RBI Banking Ombudsman

domestic_abuse.title: Domestic Abuse — What To Do
domestic_abuse.urgentNote: If you are in immediate danger, call 112 (Police) or 181 (Women's Helpline) right now. Your safety comes first.

steps.title: Ensure Your Immediate Safety
steps.description: If you're in danger right now, prioritize getting to a safe location.
details: Call 112 (Police) if you're in immediate physical danger
Call 181 (Women's Helpline) for immediate counselling and assistance — available 24/7
If possible, go to a trusted friend, family member, or neighbour
One Stop Centres (OSCs) provide shelter, medical aid, legal aid, and counselling — call 181 to find your nearest one
Keep a bag packed with essentials (ID documents, phone charger, cash, change of clothes) if you're planning to leave

steps.title: Document the Abuse
steps.description: When it's safe to do so, start documenting incidents of abuse.
details: Keep a private written log: date, time, what happened, any injuries, any witnesses
Photograph any physical injuries with a visible timestamp (turn on date stamp in camera settings)
Save threatening messages, abusive texts, and voicemails
If safe, get a medical examination and ask for a medical report documenting injuries
Keep documents safe — store them somewhere the abuser cannot access (use SafeStep's encrypted vault)
If there are witnesses, note their names and contact details

steps.title: Seek a Protection Order
steps.description: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) 2005, you can get a protection order.
details: You can apply for a Protection Order through a Protection Officer, Service Provider, or directly to a Magistrate
A Protection Order can prevent the abuser from committing further violence, entering your home, or contacting you
You do NOT need to leave your home to get a protection order — the law protects your right to live in the shared household
Free legal aid is available through the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
Contact your nearest One Stop Centre (call 181) — they can help you file for a protection order

steps.title: File a Police Complaint
steps.description: Domestic violence is a criminal offence. You have the right to file an FIR.
details: Visit your nearest police station — you can file a Zero FIR at any station
You have the right to request a female officer to record your statement
Bring your documentation: injury photos, medical reports, threatening messages
The police are legally required to register your FIR — if they refuse, you can approach the SP or a Magistrate
You can also file a complaint directly with the National Commission for Women (NCW) online

steps.title: Access Support Services
steps.description: Multiple organizations provide free support for domestic abuse survivors.
details: 181 — Women's Helpline (24/7) — counselling, shelter, legal aid
One Stop Centres (OSCs) — shelter + medical + legal + counselling under one roof
District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) — free legal representation
Shakti Shalini — specialised domestic violence support
Vandrevala Foundation — 1860-2662-345 — 24/7 mental health support
iCall TISS — 9152987821 — free counselling

workplace_harassment.title: Workplace Harassment — What To Do
workplace_harassment.urgentNote: If you are experiencing sexual harassment at work, you have legal protections under the POSH Act, 2013.

steps.title: Document Every Incident
steps.description: Keep detailed records of every harassment incident with dates, times, and witnesses.
details: Write a detailed account of each incident: date, time, location, what was said/done, who was present
Save all relevant emails, messages, and written communications
Note down names and contact details of any witnesses
If harassment is verbal, note exact words used as closely as possible
Keep records on a personal device — not on your work computer or email
Upload documents to SafeStep's Evidence Vault for timestamped preservation

steps.title: File a Complaint with the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)
steps.description: Every organization with 10+ employees must have an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act.
details: Write a formal complaint addressed to the ICC Presiding Officer
Include: detailed description of incident(s), dates, names, and evidence
You must file within 3 months of the last incident (extendable by 3 months in special circumstances)
The ICC must complete inquiry within 90 days
During the inquiry, you can request: transfer (yours or respondent's), leave, or work-from-home
If your organization doesn't have an ICC, you can file with the Local Complaints Committee (LCC)

steps.title: If No ICC — Contact the Local Complaints Committee
steps.description: If your workplace doesn't have an ICC, or you work in the informal sector, contact the District-level LCC.
details: The Local Complaints Committee (LCC) is set up at the district level
It handles complaints from workplaces with fewer than 10 employees and the informal sector
Contact your District Women and Child Development Officer to reach the LCC
The filing process and timeline is the same as with an ICC
You can also file a complaint directly with the National Commission for Women

steps.title: File a Police Complaint (If Applicable)
steps.description: For severe cases, you also have the right to file a police complaint.
details: Sexual harassment is also a criminal offence under the Indian Penal Code
You can file an FIR at any police station — this is separate from the ICC complaint
Filing a police complaint does not prevent you from also filing with the ICC (and vice versa)
You have the right to request a female officer to record your statement
For cyber-related workplace harassment, you can also file on cybercrime.gov.in

steps.title: Seek Legal and Emotional Support
steps.description: Get professional guidance and support to navigate the process.
details: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) provides free legal aid
Call 181 (Women's Helpline) for immediate counselling and guidance
iCall TISS — 9152987821 — free professional counselling
Vandrevala Foundation — 1860-2662-345 — 24/7 mental health support
Consider consulting a lawyer specializing in POSH/employment law
You are legally protected against retaliation for filing a complaint
